incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: p99 streaming latency breach detected for region-us-west-2 (model: redwood-small-v2)
incident-bot: Alerts: p95=420ms (baseline 120ms), p99=2.9s (baseline 350ms), streaming stall rate 3.6% (SLO target 0.5%) — traffic spike + increased tail. Metrics link: https://console.redwood/alerts/1777777777
emily: I'm on it. grabbing dashboards now — @raj can you join? I'm going to check host-level IO and cgroup stats.
raj: here. initial hunch: noisy tenant in shared-gpu pool, seen similar with KV cache pressure before. pulling perf and nvidia-smi.
luca: I'm pulling model QPS distribution and active prefix cache hit rate.
emily: logs: observed many short-lived pipelines with heavy prefix writes -> KV eviction spikes. host /dev/nvme* writeback backlog rising.
emily: running: `ssh gpu-host-23 sudo iostat -xz 1 3` -> high await on nvme1, util ~98%
raj: `sudo cat /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/gpu-pool/blkio.throttle.iops_device` shows bursts; also seeing cgroup write_iops throttling hit.
jia: customers? cs-alex any reports from support? which tenants affected?
cs-alex: CS ticket from tenant "BrightApps" reporting streaming stalls and failed RPCs ~10:02-10:12. They saw partial truncation of streamed chunks; severity P2 so far.
emily: ok customer impact confirmed. marking bridge. adding postmortem stub.
emily: mitigation options: 1) throttle suspected tenant concurrency (fast) 2) move tenant off noisy pool to dedicated node (evac) 3) bump cgroup write_iops temporarily (risky) 4) enable fallback lower-cost model route to reduce IO per request
raj: quick check: `nvidia-smi topo -m` shows no NVLINK issues. GPU utilization moderate, but CPU IO wait is high -> indicates storage bottleneck not compute.
luca: cache hitrate fell from 92% -> 58% for prefix store, causing extra disk reads/writes.
emily: let's throttle tenant to 30% of baseline concurrency and start migration in parallel. raj please run tenant throttle and start eviction plan.
raj: doing throttle via control plane: `redwoodctl tenant update --id brightapps --concurrency=0.3` — applied. Monitoring.
ops-bot: action logged: tenant brightapps concurrency set to 0.3 by raj at 10:06:12
emily: starting graceful eviction: `kubectl cordon gpu-host-23 && kubectl drain gpu-host-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m` — planning to move pods to dedicated pool.
raj: initiating eviction step 1: replicate critical pods to dedicated-dyn-pool, then kill originals. Command executed.
jia: notifying BrightApps: "we're throttling your workload and migrating you to a dedicated pool to restore streaming SLOs. ETA ~8-12min" — sent.
emily: observed immediate p99 drop from 2.9s -> 1.6s after throttle. streaming stall rate down to 1.2%.
luca: cache hit rate starting to recover as background evictions reduce. KV eviction rate fell 3x.
emily: migration progress: 40% pods relocated. no new OOMs. Disk writeback backlog decreasing.
raj: completed eviction, host drained. `kubectl uncordon gpu-host-23` not yet — leaving out of rotation until disk backpressure cleared.
ops-bot: host gpu-host-23 marked maintenance by raj.
emily: post-mitigation metrics: p95=150ms, p99=420ms, stalls=0.6% (still above target but improving).
jia: BrightApps reports improved behavior and resumed testing. they still see occasional small stalls but much better.
oncall-l2: taking over for mitigation verification and follow-up. I'll validate cgroup settings, ensure writeback settled, and plan permanent mitigation.
oncall-l2: suggested follow-ups: 1) enforce per-tenant persistent IO quotas (blkio controller) 2) tune KV cache eviction policy to prefer LRU with size ceiling per-tenant 3) introduce reactive routing to dedicated pools when prefix writeback exceeds threshold
emily: agree. also recommend adding a runbook entry for "kv-store writeback spike" with playbook steps we just used.
raj: I captured the exact commands and telemetry. I'll open infra ticket to add automated tenant throttling runbook
ejira: INFRA-5921 (placeholder) — raj will create.
cs-alex: final customer update draft: "We've migrated your workload to a dedicated pool and throttled concurrency to prevent further stalls. We're monitoring and will follow up with root cause and permanent fixes."
emily: switching channel: assign post-handoff checklist to oncall-l2. I'm stepping off the page. :white_check_mark:
oncall-l2: I'll keep watch and close when sustained SLO for 30m. reassigning to ops-bot for automated checks.
ops-bot: scheduled: collect p95/p99 streaming metrics every 5m for 60m; create alert if p99 > 800ms.
oncall-l2: closing live incident — mitigation applied, customers notified, handoff complete. root-cause suspected noisy-tenant IO pressure -> KV cache churn -> host writeback -> streaming stalls.
emily: thanks all. please append logs and commands to postmortem ticket and tag me for review.
incident-bot: Incident thread 1777777777 resolved (status: mitigated) at 10:45:00. Duration ~39m.
__note: This document is a single Slack thread. Messages are chronological and prefixed by sender name. No title field included per agents.md.
